look_here_first: Start with the classic bee-balm head: an aromatic perennial with opposite leaves and a dense rounded terminal head of pale lavender to pink bilabiate flowers rather than the tiered bracted whorls typical of M. citriodora and M. punctata.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pale lavender to pink bilabiate corollas

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowering head not arranged as the strongly separated stacked whorls typical of M. citriodora

lookalikes.differences: Compared with M. citriodora and M. punctata, wild bergamot usually presents a more conventional dense terminal head rather than conspicuous tiered whorls with showy bracts. Do not rely on flower color alone.
